Subject: Question on token accounting & packaging for pilot

Hi Avery,

Thanks again for the demo — excited to move forward with the BrightCart pilot. Before we sign the SOW, our finance and engineering teams flagged a few questions about how Redwood will meter the pilot so we can model costs on our side. Quick list of the things we need clarity on: 

- When we send long catalog prefixes (12–18k tokens) at the start of calls, how are those counted against the pilot minimums — per request or amortized across calls?
- For streaming responses, do you bill on final output length only or on stream chunks as they’re emitted?
- Rounding and minimums: how do you round partial-token usage and what per-call/session minimums should we expect?
- Prefix/KV reuse credit: if we reuse the same prefix 1000x across a day, is there any crediting or amortization?

I attached a spreadsheet (brightcart_prefix_samples.xlsx) with a few real examples from our system. Can you send a short written example of how a few of those calls would be billed?

Ideally we want to get this into the SOW — the commercial team is flexible but we need a deterministic model for our procurement team. CCing contracts so they can see the question.

Thanks,
Tom

Tom — thanks for the clear examples and the spreadsheet. Short answer up top, then I’ll loop in Kimberley and Sergio for the billing math and the KV-credit detail.

Summary: 
- Long prefixes: we meter the prefix tokens per request by default, but for pilots we can apply an amortization credit model (example below) so large, repeated prefixes aren’t charged fully every call.
- Streaming: billing is on the total tokens emitted (final output length), not per intermediate chunk; however, certain low-latency streaming paths may be billed with a small per-chunk overhead for highly fragmented streams.
- Rounding/minimums: hosted API uses a 50-token quantum for invoicing with a 200-token per-session minimum for streaming endpoints. We round up to the nearest quantum per-call when producing an invoice.
- KV/prefix reuse: we can apply a KV-reuse credit for identical prefixes within a 24-hour window; default pilot credit is 40% of the prefix tokens after the first call.

Action: Kimberley — can you confirm we’re comfortable proposing the 40% amortization for BrightCart’s pilot and attach a short sample calculation? Sergio — can you produce three example rows (using Tom’s sheet) showing how a) an isolated request, b) a repeated-prefix call, and c) a streaming session would bill under this model. I’ll prepare language for the SOW once we have numbers.

Thanks — Avery

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 10:03:00 -0700

Avery/Kimberly — putting the billing math here so it’s easy to paste into the SOW. I used the sample rows from brightcart_prefix_samples.xlsx and added a small CSV (billing_examples.csv). Notes on the model we discussed: 

Policy (pilot-specific):
- Metering basis: tokens = prompt_tokens + response_tokens for each request.
- Quantum (invoicing): we round billed tokens up to the nearest 50-token quantum per request (i.e., billed_units = ceil(tokens / 50) * 50).
- Streaming endpoints: billed_tokens = final_total_output_tokens + any orchestration overhead; we do NOT bill incremental stream chunks separately except when chunk_count > 16 (very fragmented), in which case we add a 20-token overhead per extra chunk beyond 16.
- Session minimum (streaming): 200-token minimum per session per-minute window (applies when sessions are kept open > 60s).
- Prefix/KV amortization (pilot): identical prefix detected within a 24h window gets a 40% credit on prompt_tokens after the first occurrence. Credits apply on a per-prefix hash basis; different prefixes are not combined.

Examples (from Tom’s sheet) — raw tokens -> billed tokens: 
1) One-off catalog lookup
   prompt 14,266 + response 120 = 14,386 tokens -> round up to 14,400 (ceil(14,386/50)*50) -> prefix amortization not applicable for single call.

2) Repeated prefix (same prefix used 12x in 24h)
   call #1: prompt 12,900 + response 150 = 13,050 -> billed 13,050 -> round to 13,050 (already multiple of 50)
   subsequent calls (2..12): prompt part credited 40% -> effective prompt = 12,900 * 0.6 = 7,740; plus response 150 = 7,890 -> round to 7,900 per call -> twelve-call bundle billed = 13,050 + 11 * 7,900 = 99,950 tokens total -> convert to units on invoice as total tokens / quantum.

3) Streaming personalization session (open 90s)
   prompt 3,100 + streamed output final 2,800, streamed in 5 chunks -> billed = 3,100 + 2,800 = 5,900 -> round to 5,900 (no per-chunk overhead). If the same session had 24 chunks, overhead = (24 - 16) * 20 = 160 extra tokens -> billed = 6,060 -> round to 6,100. Also subject to 200-token session minimum (not relevant here).

Edge behavior / rounding notes: 
- Our invoice system aggregates over invoice period; you may see multiple rounded items aggregated. We do not re-round aggregated totals; rounding occurs at the line-item level (per-request) then sums.
- For pilot billing we can present both the raw token totals and the post-amortization billed totals for transparency.

I attached billing_examples.csv with the example rows and per-line math. If we want an alternate amortization (e.g., 50% credit or a fixed amortized token allowance per prefix) I can regenerate the CSV quickly.

—Sergio
Sergio Alvarez

- Pricing: 20% standard pilot discount on hosted API list rates.
- Billing model: per-request metering with 50-token quantum rounding and a 200-token streaming session minimum.
- Prefix amortization: 40% credit on identical prefixes within a 24h window (applies after the first invocation).
- Trial concession: first 30 days we’ll waive 50% of billed session-minimum charges to reduce your early pilot costs.
